lead: Finite-amplitude relative-entropy curvature bound for overdamped diffusions

claims.exact_statement: For smooth overdamped diffusion dX=Fdt+sqrt(2T)dW with smooth positive stationary density rho and stationary velocity u=F-T grad(log rho), the small relative-density perturbation p=rho(1+phi) has curvature difference xi=-2T<alpha u.grad(phi)>_rho, alpha=Delta(phi)+grad(log rho).grad(phi), and sigma>=xi^2/(4 T^3 <alpha^2 |grad(phi)|^2>_rho), under the source's decay and perturbation assumptions.

costs.observations: short-time density relaxation and equilibrium reference curvature
costs.precision: derivative and spatial-field estimation costs are not bounded by theorem

claims.next_gate: None for this source reconstruction; it is the baseline only.

claims.exact_statement: Under the exact model/interface in DERIVATION.md, for any smooth strictly positive normalized f with all displayed derivatives/integrals finite, define G_f=-2 L_0 f/(T f)+|grad f|^2/f^2, Q_f=<G_f^2 |grad f|^2>_rho, xi=D''_NESS(0)-D''_eq(0), and sigma=T^-1<|u|^2>_rho. Then xi=T<u.(G_f grad f)>_rho exactly, and Q_f>0 implies sigma>=xi^2/(T^3 Q_f). No smallness condition on ||f-1||_infinity is used.
assumptions: u=F-T grad(log rho) and div(rho u)=0
same initial p0=rho f and common relative-entropy reference rho
equilibrium comparison drift F_eq=T grad(log rho)
f smooth strictly positive and normalized
integrations by parts and two time derivatives are valid
